# `Q-5-24` — Two Pages Claim the Same Alias

> Two pages declare `aliases:` entries that resolve to the same
> redirect, so only one of them could take effect.

## What this means

A redirect can only send visitors to one place. When two pages
both claim an old URL, there is no way to honour both, and no way
to guess which author is right.

```yaml
# guides/deploying.qmd
aliases:
  - /deploy.html

# reference/deploy-api.qmd
aliases:
  - /deploy.html      # same old URL, different page
```

## Fragments make this subtler

An alias may carry a fragment, and several pages *may* share one
redirect file as long as they claim different fragments:

```yaml
# building.qmd
aliases:
  - /hub/              # owns the bare URL
  - /hub/#image

# deploying.qmd
aliases:
  - /hub/#deploy       # fine: a different fragment
```

That is allowed, and both fragments route to their own page.

This error still fires in two cases:

- **Two pages claim the same fragment**, including the
  fragment-less one (as in the first example).
- **No page claims the bare URL.** If `building.qmd` above dropped
  its `/hub/` entry, both remaining aliases would be fragments,
  and a visitor arriving at plain `/hub/` would have no defined
  destination. Rather than pick one arbitrarily, Quarto asks you
  to say which page owns it.

## How to fix it

Remove the alias from all but one page. If several pages really do
descend from one old page, choose the one a visitor should land on
by default and give it the fragment-less alias; the others keep
their fragment-qualified entries.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 does not report this at all. The last page processed wins
and overwrites the earlier redirect, so which page a visitor
reaches depends on file-processing order — and the author whose
alias lost is never told.
